note: Honest counts, not aspirations. Every number below was measured, not chosen. A count may fall and may not rise; see qa/README.md for how to re-derive all of it in one command.

policy.why_a_ratchet_and_not_a_fix: The live totals are in `lint.total` and `format.unformatted_files` below; they are the only numbers in this file that should be quoted as current. Running `ruff format .` or `ruff check --fix .` would rewrite ~240 files this worker does not own, across ten workers and eight domain leads, and make the wave unmergeable; a reformat is also indistinguishable from a semantic edit in review. Deleting the rules that fire would be a lie. So: freeze the real number per rule per tree, publish it, refuse an increase.
policy.snapshot_caveat: Taken while ten workers were writing to the same tree. The count moved 793 -> 820 in about twelve minutes on 2026-08-10 as packages/trappoint-testkit/ landed. Re-take once on the merge commit with --rebaseline and quote the result in the PR body; after that this is a gate rather than a snapshot. See qa/README.md.
policy.hard_gate: A (rule, tree) pair recorded at 0 is a hard gate: the first finding fails the build. A pair absent from `lint.rules` also defaults to 0, so a rule that has never fired in a tree is gated there too.

zero_tolerance.why: ruff.toml's preamble calls these load-bearing for the Apache substrate: a blanket except is how a refusal becomes a silence; print() outside a CLI is diagnostic output no ledger will contain; bandit findings reach the provisioning and conformance paths; a naive datetime in an evidentiary payload is an unanswerable question under cross-examination; TRY300/RET hide which branch produced a refusal.
